summary: Ch.1: Akari, an 18-year-old first-year in Kyoto, breaks down crying after losing his new wallet; a stranger (Touma) comforts him and helps him search. Next day they meet again: Touma is in the same faculty and year. They eat lunch together (Touma orders the canteen's weird dish), meet Akari's friends Anzu and Mamesuke, and Touma asks Akari to show him around Kyoto. On their outing near Kiyomizu, Touma tells him crying was proof he was trying hard, helps a tourist in fluent English, says he is glad he spoke to Akari, and admits he worried about making friends. Akari offers to help tidy Touma's messy flat; both look forward to tomorrow.

Ch.2: Akari sees off his little brother You and You's friend Kuranosuke (Mamesuke's brother). At the campus café Touma and Mamesuke talk; Mamesuke worries Akari can't say no and thanks Touma for befriending him (Akari gave Mamesuke his nickname). Akari agrees to do a classmate's chore; Touma finds him and helps so they finish early. Akari takes Touma to his favourite omurice place, a bakery and the river's turtle stepping-stones; a kite steals Akari's bun and Touma shares his. Touma says they complement each other. Akari forgets to collect the teacher's birthday cake; Touma fetches it, glad Akari relied on him, saying it makes him feel special. Akari realises he takes Touma's presence for granted and vows to remember Touma's birthday (6 Dec), which Touma himself forgot.

Ch.3: End of the first term. Touma, who refused every Gion festival invitation, asks Akari not to go either and invites him on a trip instead; they go to Kibune to escape the heat (a pricey riverside restaurant, flowing somen, a matchmaking shrine). Akari tells Touma that since meeting him he has come to like himself. Touma shares his past: a lonely childhood with busy parents, being called scary, studying only to please them, picking Kyoto on a whim -- and that he first noticed Akari helping a lost stranger at entrance day and wanted to be his friend, maybe fate. He asks Akari to call him by his name. On the train home Akari falls asleep on his shoulder; Touma thinks: 'I'm really glad.'
